citation: West, M. L. (2007). Indo-European Poetry and Myth. Oxford University Press.
notes: n. 25: sun and moon called the eyes of Dyaus; the Vedic dual phrase matches Greek etymologically but not semantically, and Latvian 'in part'.

citation: West, M. L. (2007). Indo-European Poetry and Myth. Oxford University Press.

citation: West, M. L. (2007). Indo-European Poetry and Myth. Oxford University Press.
notes: Vedic-Greek: 'broad' + 'seat' of earth. Homeric εὐρυοδείης suspected to replace older *εὐρυεδείης (starred Greek form, not PIE; n. 53 Schmitt).

citation: West, M. L. (2007). Indo-European Poetry and Myth. Oxford University Press.
notes: Graeco-Aryan theme: earth 'bearing' all, same verb (*bher-, not printed by West) in Avestan and Greek. West gives no PIE phrase.
